key_insight: PyroDash lets a small language model decide token-by-token when to hand off difficult reasoning to a frozen large model, reducing LLM usage while keeping strong math performance.
engineering_relevance: It offers a practical, cost-aware inference design for scalable reasoning systems by internalizing routing inside the SLM and avoiding separate routers, LLM retraining, or LLM logit access.
method: SLM emits a control token to request LLM assistance during generation.
A Collaborate Engine sends the query plus partial reasoning trace to the frozen LLM for a single completion handoff.
Training uses three stages: control-token embedding learning, offloading-oriented supervised fine-tuning, and cost-aware alignment with Group Relative Policy Optimization.
evidence_signal: Across five mathematical reasoning benchmarks, PyroDash trades off accuracy and cost; at λ=0.05 it reaches 64.04% average accuracy with 20.4% lower cost, and at λ=0.6 it cuts cost from USD 49.36 to USD 1.78.
watch_item: Performance depends on the learned control-token policy, so miscalibrated handoffs or distribution shifts could increase LLM calls or reduce reasoning accuracy.
paper_title: PyroDash: Cost-Efficient Token-Level Small-Large Language Model Collaborative Inference
